description: Analyze an ingested book and generate a set of 'ultra high probability' exam questions tied to a user-provided curriculum. Produces a structured book analysis (summary, key concepts, topic outline) and a ranked question set where each question carries a probability/importance score and links back to source concepts. Uses the LLMProvider from FEAT-002 (mock works keyless). Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: Create src/lib/analyze/analyzeBook.ts: given a bookId (chunks from the store) and optional curriculum text/keywords, call the LLMProvider to produce a BookAnalysis: { summary, keyConcepts: [{ concept, importance, sourceChunkIndexes }], topicOutline }. Map/reduce across chunks so long books are handled without exceeding context; merge per-chunk results into a deduplicated concept list.

Create src/lib/analyze/generateQuestions.ts: given the BookAnalysis + curriculum, produce ranked exam questions: [{ id, question, answer, concept, questionType (recall|application|conceptual), probability (0-1 'exam likelihood' score), rationale }]. 'Probability' should be derived from concept importance + curriculum overlap; document the scoring heuristic. Support requesting N questions.
Define the curriculum input model: accept either a pasted curriculum/syllabus text or a list of topics; store it alongside the book. Add zod schemas.

Create POST /api/analyze route handler (src/app/api/analyze/route.ts): body { bookId, curriculum }, runs analyzeBook then generateQuestions, persists analysis + questions to the store, returns them. Validate with zod.
Create GET /api/books/[bookId] route to fetch stored analysis + questions for display.

Build a book results UI at src/app/books/[bookId]/page.tsx: show the analysis summary, key concepts, and the ranked question list sorted by probability descending, each with its score, type, and answer (collapsible). Include a curriculum input on the upload/analyze flow.

Add unit tests under src/lib/analyze/__tests__: analyzeBook returns non-empty concepts from sample chunks via MockProvider; generateQuestions returns the requested count with probability values in [0,1] sorted descending; curriculum overlap raises the probability of matching concepts.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/analyze with a valid bookId returns a BookAnalysis plus a non-empty ranked question array.
Each generated question has a probability in [0,1] and the returned list is sorted by probability descending.
Providing curriculum topics that overlap book concepts increases those questions' probability (verified by unit test).
The full analyze->questions flow works end-to-end with the MockProvider (no AI key).
All new unit tests pass and `npm run build` succeeds.
verification: source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && npm run typecheck
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && npm run build
findings: Implemented src/lib/analyze/{types,analyzeBook,generateQuestions}.ts, POST /api/analyze, GET /api/books/[bookId], and the src/app/books/[bookId]/page.tsx results UI (curriculum input + collapsible answers). Added AnalysisResult + saveAnalysis to the BookStore interface and in-memory impl; StoredBook now carries optional curriculum/analysis/questions/analyzedAt. FEAT-003 introduces its OWN richer BookAnalysis (summary, keyConcepts[{concept, importance, sourceChunkIndexes}], topicOutline) in src/lib/analyze/types.ts rather than the primitive BookAnalysis in src/lib/llm/types.ts (which the MockProvider.completeJSON still returns). Scoring heuristics are documented in the source: analyzeBook importance = normalised cross-chunk frequency + 0.3 curriculum boost (capped at 1); generateQuestions probability = clamp01(0.6*importance + 0.4*curriculumOverlap). NOTE ON MOCK BEHAVIOUR: MockProvider.completeJSON derives keywords per chunk via top-N term frequency, so a term appearing in multiple chunks is not guaranteed to be in every chunk's keyword list; the provenance test was written to assert sourceChunkIndexes is a non-empty subset of the input chunk indexes rather than the exact set. Question types are assigned deterministically by rotating recall/application/conceptual (no model call needed). ESLint (Next core-web-vitals) enforces react-hooks/set-state-in-effect: the book page effect must not call a setState-containing function synchronously; solved by a pure fetchBook() helper whose results are applied inside the effect's async .then callback. All verification passed keyless: npm test (31 tests), npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run build.
